targetName: Space Shuttle launch stack (Discovery on pad)

terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: multi-body crewed launch vehicle stack (winged orbiter + propellant tank + two solid boosters)
motionPotential: separable stage bodies (boosters and tank detach from orbiter)
hinged payload bay doors on the orbiter
materialFamilies: sprayed insulation foam (matte dielectric, saturated orange)
heat-treated metal (metallic, mid roughness) at nozzles
objectClass.notes: Read by direct inspection of the reference; see _shuttle/analysis/image-analysis.md. Not a character or hybrid, so no anatomy track applies.

reasoning: Four macro bodies, not one: tank, two boosters, orbiter. A single-root spec would be shallow by construction.
Occlusion risk is the dominant score. One night view shows one side. The far side of the stack, the orbiter ventral surface and the payload bay interior are never observed.
Silhouette is complex but every sub-form is a primitive: ogive, cylinder, cone, extruded delta, lofted fuselage. No organic or implicit surface is required.
Repetition is real but low-count: booster case joint rings, the cabin window group, elevon split lines.
Action readiness is required by the host page, which explodes the stack and makes each component clickable.
Tier is complex rather than ultra-complex: a 400 x 492 reference cannot support an ultra-complex micro-detail bar.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Nose-to-barrel transition ring where the ogive meets the cylindrical barrel.
Vertical conduit line running the full length of the tank, offset from the centreline; reads as a raised narrow ridge casting its own shadow.
Waisted band of different surface treatment between the two tank barrels, at a slightly smaller radius.
Raised circumferential joint rings dividing each booster into case segments. A repetition system, not one-off geometry.
Booster nose is two cone angles: a steeper cap over a shallower frustum, with a step between them.
Aft skirt flares to a larger diameter than the case barrel.
Near-black nose cap distinct from the white fuselage, with a hard boundary.
Cluster of bright window rectangles on the crew module, arranged in two bands.
Dark swept band along each wing leading edge, forming a shallow V outward from the fuselage.
Split line across each wing trailing edge separating inboard from outboard elevon.
Wing planform is double-delta: a shallow-sweep glove ahead of a steeper-sweep outer panel, with a visible break.
USA plus flag on one wing upper surface, NASA plus Discovery on the other. Placement observed, glyphs below resolution.
Two raised pods flanking the fin base at the aft end of the fuselage.
Three bell nozzles clustered at the aft end, one high and two low.
Forward strut standing the orbiter nose off the tank, leaving a visible gap between the two bodies.
The leading-edge band is the only lower-roughness response on the vehicle; every other surface is matte. Recorded so the material pass does not flatten it.

anatomy.note: primaryDomain is object, so no anatomy track applies.

definitionOfDone: Silhouette, body proportions and inter-body placement match the reference within perspective error.
All four macro bodies are separate, named, clickable and explodable, and carry the host page group names.
Each of the fifteen detail-inventory entries is realised as geometry or a material override, never prose alone.
Material response separates matte foam, matte tile, matte paint and metallic nozzle, with no albedo reuse across channels.
The model holds up from at least four viewpoints, including the two the reference never shows.
Every unobserved region is reported as inference rather than presented as measured.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: surface looks like flat plastic
local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

featureGroups.name: Inter-body proportions and placement
qualityCriteria: Tank diameter, booster diameter, orbiter span and body lengths hold the measured ratios.
Booster nose apexes sit below the tank nose apex.
Wing tips extend beyond the outer envelope of the boosters.
failureModes: boosters modelled as tall as the tank
wing span shrunk inside the booster envelope
orbiter mounted on the tank centreline instead of standing off on one side

featureGroups.name: Orbiter identity features
qualityCriteria: Double-delta planform with a visible sweep break.
Dark nose cap and dark wing leading-edge band with hard boundaries.
Fin, both pods and three nozzles present at the aft end.
failureModes: single-sweep delta wing
leading edge left white
engine cluster reduced to one nozzle

featureGroups.name: Honest reporting of unobserved regions
qualityCriteria: Every region the single view cannot show is labelled inference in the spec and in the summary.
failureModes: far side presented as measured
payload bay interior claimed from the photo

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
booster-to-tank contact and radial placement delta
dark-region boundary placement delta at nose cap, leading edges and engine bay

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match

stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Far side of the stack is unobserved; reconstructed from the assembly bilateral symmetry and the rotational symmetry of tank and boosters. RESOLVED: build symmetric, report as inference.
Orbiter ventral surface faces the tank and is never visible. RESOLVED: dark insulation from published layout, reported as inference.
Payload bay interior is closed in the reference. RESOLVED: plain bay volume behind hinged doors, reported as inference.
Cabin window count and spacing are below the resolution floor. RESOLVED: published layout, confidence 0.55.
Marking glyph forms are unreadable. RESOLVED: placement from the reference, letterforms approximated on a canvas texture.

Absolute albedo is unrecoverable from a night frame. RESOLVED: white-patch de-lighting recovers chromaticity; values are directionally right, not photometric. Measured illuminant is near-neutral, so the earlier sodium-tint assumption was dropped.
Aft orbiter-to-tank attach structure is occluded. RESOLVED: published configuration, confidence 0.4.
Scale anchor is the host page hotspot contract (tank radius 4.6 units = 4.2 m), not the photo. The photo independently agrees within 4 percent on wing span, which is the cross-check, not the source.

Material extraction passed its deterministic gate on all seven regions, but three crops (dark insulation, nozzle metal, glazing) are contaminated by chroma bleed or shadow. Their extracted albedo is rejected in favour of the de-lit authored value, and the rejection is recorded on each material.

Wing trailing edge and elevon split; fin seen edge-on; engine cluster; booster aft skirts.
Nose cap boundary, cabin window bands, dark band sweeping aft from the forward fuselage.

featureReviews.note: Tank, booster diameters and booster-to-tank placement read correctly, and the booster apexes sit below the tank apex as measured. But the orbiter reads oversized against the tank because its wing starts far too high, so the tank is hidden along the mid body where the reference shows orange on both sides of the fuselage.

Wing leading edge is anchored at x=9.0, level with the crew module. The reference puts the visible wing in the bottom quarter of the vehicle. Root cause: the dark swept band behind the cabin was read as the wing glove leading edge during spec authoring, when re-measurement puts it at x 8.1 to 11.4 spanning only z +-3.2, which is forward-fuselage width, not wing span. It is a tile boundary on the fuselage, not the wing.

The orbiter renders almost uniformly white. Nose cap, wing leading-edge band and the fuselage tile boundary are all present in the spec and in code but none of them read. The leading-edge boxes are 1.00 units tall against a 0.95-unit wing at the same centre, so they are effectively coincident and only 0.31 units protrude forward, which is about 2 px at review scale.
The two-slope profile is built and the step exists, but the cap is too long and too pointed. The reference nose is blunter.

Ogive curve and the transition ring read correctly. The cable tray ridge is on the far side at this azimuth so it cannot be judged here. Tank albedo renders as pale tan rather than the deep burnt orange of the reference.

Three nozzles, body flap and mount are present and correctly placed between the booster skirts. The manoeuvring pods do not read at all from this azimuth and the fin is edge-on, which matches the reference, so this feature needs an orbit view to judge properly.

reviewHistory.summary: Silhouette reads as a Shuttle launch stack and the deterministic gates pass (silhouette IoU 0.9426, no degenerate view across four azimuths), but AI vision on the comparison sheet finds three critical failures. (1) The wing is anchored far too far forward: its leading edge starts level with the crew module where the reference puts the visible wing in the bottom quarter. Re-measuring the dark swept band behind the cabin gives x 8.1 to 11.4 over z +-3.2, which is forward-fuselage width, so it is a fuselage tile boundary and not the wing glove leading edge as assumed at spec time. (2) No dark region reads at all: nose cap, leading-edge band and tile boundary are built but the leading-edge geometry is coincident with the wing surface and only 0.31 units protrude. (3) Tank albedo renders pale tan instead of deep burnt orange. The passing IoU is framing-dominated, exactly the photo-vs-procedural miscalibration the self-correction reference warns about: both images are a bright vertical vehicle centred on black, so the gate measures composition, not fidelity.

Secondary pad floodlight separating the boosters from the black sky.

lightingFromPhoto.groundContact: The stack is shown free-standing on the page, so a soft elliptical ground shadow anchors it. The reference has no visible ground shadow: the pad deck is unlit.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Night sky contributes almost nothing; kept only to stop the shadow side reading as a hole. The page renders on a light background, so the shipped lighting lifts fill above the reference value on purpose. Stated rather than silently changed.

proceduralStrategy: Lathe every surface of revolution from an explicit profile: tank ogive, aft dome, booster nose, skirt flare, nozzle bells.
Extrude the wing and fin from a planform polygon with an aerofoil section, so the sweep break is real geometry.
Loft the orbiter fuselage across stations rather than stacking boxes.
Instance the repetition systems (joint rings, windows, elevons) instead of authoring each copy.
Generate all linework and markings as canvas textures at runtime; the page must work with no network.
Name every mesh with the host page group ids so the existing layer buttons and hotspots keep working.

component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
